subject.title: resolveCliAuthEpoch invalidates every live CLI session when local credential source-of-storage flips, even though identity is unchanged

question: What should be the Claude CLI auth identity boundary for reusable sessions when an OpenClaw auth profile exists but the local Claude credential source appears or disappears?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the repair can either preserve sessions across a cosmetic storage flip or accidentally preserve them across an unproven credential identity change, so maintainer security/product intent is required before automation changes the boundary.

options.title: Adopt a narrow identity-stable fix
options.body: Make Claude CLI auth epochs ignore storage-shape churn only when the implementation can prove unchanged identity, with tests for storage flips, logout, and real account changes.

options.title: Keep fail-closed behavior
options.body: Leave the current epoch composition in place and document that users may see resets when credential sources churn because identity cannot be proven safely.

options.title: Choose a host-identity model
options.body: Require an identity-bearing host Claude credential fingerprint and coordinate the overlapping PRs around that internal contract instead of profile-canonical behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt a narrow identity-stable fix
recommendation.body: Make Claude CLI auth epochs ignore storage-shape churn only when the implementation can prove unchanged identity, with tests for storage flips, logout, and real account changes.

likelyOwner.reason: The initial auth invalidation behavior and current session-reuse boundary trace to steipete's commit history, and the open question is an auth/session policy call.
